## 1. Learning objectives
After this lesson you can:
- explain what a **class** (blueprint) and an **object** (one thing made from it) are;
- write a class with **fields**, a **constructor** and **methods**, and use `this`;
- create objects with `new` and read or change their fields with the dot (`rice.quantity`);
- explain why two variables can point at the same object, and what `null` means;
- read the new `Product` class and the `Inventory` that now keeps a list of products.

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- In lessons 03-08 one product was spread over **four places**: a name in one list, a price in a map, a quantity in
  another map, a reorder level in a third. To know everything about "Rice 25kg" you had to look in four places.
  A **class** puts them together in one place.
- A **class** is a blueprint, like the printed form for a stock card. An **object** is one filled-in card.
  `new Product("Rice 25kg", 125050, 10)` makes one object. You can make as many as you like; each one keeps
  its own values.
- **Fields** are the variables inside a class (`name`, `priceCentavos`, `quantity`, `reorderLevel`).
  **Methods** are the things an object can do (`status()`, `receive(5)`, `sell(2)`).
- A **constructor** is a special method with the same name as the class and no return type. It runs once for every
  `new` and sets the starting values. Inside it, `this` means "the object being built", so `this.name = name;`
  copies the parameter into the field.
- You reach into an object with a dot: `rice.quantity` is the quantity field of the `rice` object, and
  `rice.status()` calls its method.
- A variable of a class type does **not** hold the object. It holds a *reference* (an address) to it.
  `Item alias = rice;` copies the address, not the object, so changing `alias` changes `rice`. A reference
  that points at nothing is `null`; using the dot on `null` crashes with a `NullPointerException`.
- `toString()` is the method Java calls when you print an object or join it to text. We write our own so
  that a `Product` prints something useful. `@Override` tells the compiler "I mean to replace the built-in one".
- **An intentional refactor.** Lessons 07-08 built `Inventory` from an `ArrayList` of names plus three `HashMap`s.
  In this lesson we **rewrite the inside** of `Inventory` to hold one `ArrayList<Product>`. The outside (its method
  names, `-1` and `false` results) is unchanged on purpose, so every old test, including the menu tests, must still pass.
  That is how professionals change code safely: tests first, then restructure. Two things become unnecessary and are
  **removed**: `StockUpdater` (the parallel-array helpers; `Product.receive` and `Product.sell` replace them) and the
  array versions of `StockReport.build` / `totalValue` (they now take a list of products).
- For now the fields are `public` so you can see the dot at work. That is not good practice; lesson 10 fixes it.

## 3. Runnable sample code
`examples/ClassesDemo.java` makes two `Item` objects, changes them, shows an alias and a `null`.
Run from the repo root:
```
java lessons/09-classes-and-objects/examples/ClassesDemo.java
```
The heart of it:
```java
Item rice = new Item("Rice 25kg", 12);
Item sugar = new Item("Sugar 1kg", 0);
rice.quantity = rice.quantity - 2;   // change ONE object's field with the dot
sugar.restock(24);                   // or call a method on it
Item alias = rice;                   // not a copy: a second name for the SAME object
```

3. **TODO 2 — `receive(amount)` and `sell(amount)`**: `receive` adds to `quantity`. `sell` refuses (returns `false`,
   changes nothing) when `amount` is more than `quantity`; otherwise it subtracts and returns `true`.
4. **TODO 3 — `StockReport.build` and `totalValue`**: loop `for (Product product : products)`. The header line and the

5. Run `../../../mvnw test`. When everything is green, read `Inventory.java` and find every place that used to
   look in `quantities.get(stored)` and now says `product.quantity`.
6. Run the app (section 6). It behaves exactly as in lesson 08 and prints `Version 0.9 - Classes and objects`.

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `NullPointerException` | Using the dot on a variable that is `null` (for example `findProduct` found nothing) | Check `if (product == null)` first |
| `name` is always `null` or `quantity` is 0 after the constructor | Wrote `name = name;` (assigns the parameter to itself) | Write `this.name = name;` |
| `non-static ... cannot be referenced from a static context` | Called an object method like `Product.receive(5)` on the class | Call it on an object: `rice.receive(5)` |
| Changing one product changes another | Two variables point at the **same** object (`Product b = a;`) | Make a second one with `new Product(...)` |
| `Product` prints as `Product@1b6d3586` | No `toString()` | Add the `toString()` method with `@Override` |
| `missing return statement` | A branch of `sell` does not return | Return `false` for the not-enough case and `true` at the end |
